prompt: A service key is compiled into the planner. Who can read it?

choices.text: The team, since the binary is minified
choices.why: Minifying removes whitespace, not strings; grep found it in one command.

choices.text: Nobody, if it is encoded in base64 first
choices.why: Encoding changes the command used to find it, and nothing else.

choices.text: Anybody who downloads the app
choices.why: Right. Treat it as published on the day the app reaches the store.

choices.text: Whoever roots the phone first and digs through it
choices.why: No root is needed: the app's package is a download anybody can unpack.

prompt: app.ts never read `tipsApiKey`. Why was the key in dist/app.js anyway?

choices.text: The build embeds the whole configuration it reads
choices.why: Right. A key anywhere in what the build reads ships, used or not.

choices.text: A bug in bundle.ts that a real bundler would not have
choices.why: Real builds do the same with BuildConfig, Info.plist and EXPO_PUBLIC_ variables.

choices.text: Node copies the JSON files it sees into the bundle
choices.why: bundle.ts copied config.json on purpose, as a build does.

choices.text: grep reads the source as well
choices.why: It read dist/app.js and nothing else.

prompt: What does the planner gain by moving the tips key to its own server? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: the key is no longer in anything a person downloads
choices.why: It lives in the server's environment.

choices.text: requests can be refused to people not signed in
choices.why: The server checks the access token first.

choices.text: the key can change without a store release
choices.why: Only the server knows it.

choices.text: the app can work with no network
choices.why: A tip still needs a request; this is about where the key lives.

prompt: Where does the lesson keep the refresh token on a phone?

choices.text: In SharedPreferences or UserDefaults, beside the settings
choices.why: Preferences are plain files in the sandbox and go into backups.

choices.text: In the database, encrypted with the data key
choices.why: The keystore is the place for it; it is the account's key.

choices.text: Nowhere; it is asked for each time
choices.why: Then the person would type the password each time.

choices.text: In the platform's Keystore or Keychain
choices.why: Right. In the course, keystore/ stands in for them.

prompt: What does rotating the refresh token buy?

choices.text: Shorter requests
choices.why: The size is the same.

choices.text: A copied refresh token works once at most, and its reuse shows
choices.why: Right. Each use spends the old one and returns a new one.

choices.text: No need for an access token
choices.why: The access token is still sent on every request.

choices.text: The password can be kept on the phone instead
choices.why: The password is typed once and kept nowhere.

prompt: Put in order what the client did for `node client.ts tip guitar` after the pause.
items: sent the request with the access token
spent the refresh token for a new pair
sent the request again and got a 200

prompt: A person signs out in a tunnel, with no network. What does the lesson say the planner does?

choices.text: Refuses to sign out until the server confirms the revoke
choices.why: The person expects to be signed out now.

choices.text: Wipes now, and queues the revoke
choices.why: Right. The revoke goes in the outbox; the wipe does not wait.

choices.text: Signs out, and keeps the data for when the network returns
choices.why: Keeping it leaves one person's data for the next.

choices.text: Deletes the server's copy of the sessions
choices.why: Signing out is not deleting the account.

prompt: In the lesson's server, how many seconds does an access token live when ACCESS_TTL is not set?
What does the lesson ask of each field the planner keeps or sends?

choices.text: Could it be useful one day?
choices.why: That question keeps everything.

choices.text: Does the store's form have a box for it?
choices.why: The form follows from what is kept, not the other way round.

choices.text: Is it encrypted on the way to the server?
choices.why: That matters, and it is a different question.

choices.text: What breaks if it is not there?
choices.why: Right. If nothing breaks, it is not needed.

prompt: The fixed log line says `sync failed for account acc-0193: session s5`. Why is that enough to fix a sync?

choices.text: The ids say which rows to look at
choices.why: Right, and the data is on the server for whoever may look.

choices.text: Because sync failures need no investigation
choices.why: They do; the ids are what the investigation needs.

choices.text: Because the crash reporter adds the e-mail address itself
choices.why: That would be the same leak by another road.

choices.text: Because the notes are in the id
choices.why: An id carries no data about the person.

prompt: The lesson finds the leaked address with `___ -E -o '[a-z.]+@[a-z.]+' app.log`.
Sessions stay in the planner's local database and are never sent anywhere. Do the stores count them as collected?

choices.text: Yes: anything the app stores is collected
choices.why: Both stores draw the line at leaving the device.

choices.text: On Google Play, not on the App Store
choices.why: Apple draws the same line.

choices.text: No, not until they leave the device
choices.why: Right. The day the outbox sends them, they go on the form.

choices.text: If they are encrypted on the phone with a data key the Keystore wraps
choices.why: Encryption does not change whether data is collected.

prompt: Match each item to the store that asks for it.

pairs.left: whether data is linked to the person and used for tracking

prompt: The planner adds a crash reporter that sends the device model with each report. What does the lesson say about the forms?

choices.text: It collects on the app's behalf, so the answers must change
choices.why: Right. One new library can make last month's answers false.

choices.text: The privacy manifest changes, and the forms stay
choices.why: The Data safety form and the App Privacy details change too.

choices.text: The model is not personal data, so it is left off
choices.why: Device data is among the types both forms list.

choices.text: Nothing changes: the library declares itself
choices.why: The store counts the library's collection as the app's.

prompt: A team hides its key by splitting it in two strings and joining them at run time. What does the lesson's reasoning say they bought?

choices.text: A key the store cannot reject
choices.why: The store is not the threat here.

choices.text: Safety from grep, which is how keys are found
choices.why: grep is one tool of many; running the app reveals the joined key.

choices.text: A different command to find it, and nothing else
choices.why: Right. The app has to use the key, so the app can be made to show it.

choices.text: The same protection as the Keystore gives
choices.why: The Keystore never hands the key to the app at all.

prompt: What did `node client.ts signout` do in the lesson's run? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: asked the server to revoke the refresh token
choices.why: POST /revoke -> 200 in the server's log.

choices.text: removed the keystore, the database and the cache
choices.why: It printed each one.

choices.text: deleted the account on the server
choices.why: Signing out is not deleting the account.

choices.text: kept the access token for the next sign-in
choices.why: The next request got a 401.

prompt: Why does the lesson put deciding about unsent outbox sessions to the person at sign-out?

choices.text: The outbox cannot be wiped
choices.why: It can; the question is whether it should be.

choices.text: Wiping loses work; keeping leaves her data to the next person
choices.why: Right. Both are costs only she can weigh, so the planner says how many there are.

choices.text: The stores require a confirmation dialog at each sign-out
choices.why: No store rule is involved.

choices.text: The server deletes them anyway
choices.why: The server never received them.

prompt: Which required-reason API category does the lesson's privacy manifest give the reason E174.1?

choices.text: UserDefaults
choices.why: That one gets CA92.1.

choices.text: The keyboards installed on the phone
choices.why: The planner does not call it.

choices.text: The system's boot time, used to measure how long the phone has been on
choices.why: The planner does not call it.

choices.text: Disk space
choices.why: Right: checking there is room before writing, as lesson 18 did.
